prisoner.name: Sitawa Nantambu Jamaa
prisoner.description: Sitawa Nantambu Jamaa, also known as Ronnie N. Dewberry, is a California prison organizer and a principal negotiator in the Prisoner Human Rights Movement. Already imprisoned on a murder conviction, he challenged prolonged solitary confinement linked to a disputed Black Guerrilla Family classification. He helped organize the 2011 and 2013 hunger strikes and the 2012 Agreement to End Hostilities, and was a plaintiff in Ashker v. Brown. He left long-term solitary confinement in October 2015 but remained imprisoned; his supporters reported that he came home on February 14, 2024. The cases below concern segregation connected to his political activity, rather than treating his entire earlier criminal sentence as activism-related custody.

cases.charges: Administrative segregation under a disputed Black Guerrilla Family classification
cases.sentence: More than 30 years in solitary confinement across California prisons. Jamaa’s sworn 2013 declaration describes continued isolation based on alleged associations and political materials. His 2016 account dates the initial placement at San Quentin to May 15, 1985, and departure from long-term solitary to October 11, 2015; he arrived at Salinas Valley general population on October 13. This was administrative confinement within an existing sentence, not a new criminal conviction. The end of solitary was not release from prison.

cases.charges: Administrative segregation after an alleged contraband discovery; political retaliation alleged
cases.sentence: Jamaa reports placement in Salinas Valley administrative segregation on January 11, 2018, and continued confinement through at least January 30. He alleged that officials fabricated contraband reports in retaliation for his role in the Ashker litigation. His March 2018 account describes two classification hearings and an extension pending a disciplinary hearing. The final disposition and segregation exit date remain unverified. These are his allegations, not an established judicial finding.

case_research.custody_evidence: Sworn 2013 declaration establishes 28 years already spent in solitary and specific political-material grounds for retention. Later first-person account establishes 1985 placement and 2015 exit from long-term solitary.
First-person account follows actual confinement from January 11 through January 30, 2018; this is multi-day segregation, not merely a threatened disciplinary penalty.

entries.custody_evidence: Two distinct segregation episodes associated with political education and prison organizing. Formal BGF membership is not inferred from the disputed classification. Prison release in 2024 is described separately.

prisoner.name: Paul Alwyn Redd Jr.
prisoner.description: Paul Alwyn Redd Jr. was an Oakland-born jailhouse lawyer, writer and prison organizer associated with the Short Corridor Collective. He participated in the movement against prolonged solitary confinement and was a plaintiff in Ashker v. Brown. His legal work helped other incarcerated people challenge prison conditions and classifications. He was released from prison in May 2020 after his murder conviction was reduced to manslaughter with credit for time served, and continued advocating for resentencing and prison reform. He died on June 19, 2022. The case recorded here concerns continued segregation based on contested political and association evidence, rather than assigning his entire underlying criminal sentence to activism.

cases.charges: Continued administrative segregation after a disputed 2011 gang-status review
cases.sentence: Redd’s sworn May 2013 declaration describes denial of inactive status in 2011 and continued confinement at Pelican Bay SHU. He said the review relied on political writings, George Jackson and Black Panther artwork, association evidence and disputed informant claims. He reported 33 of the previous 35 years in solitary, including a break from Pelican Bay between December 2000 and March 2001. This case records the documented continuation of segregation, not a new criminal conviction or an uninterrupted 35-year term. The individual exit date for this segregation episode is unresolved.

case_research.custody_evidence: Sworn testimony describes ongoing SHU confinement from the 2011 retention decision through May 2013 and the political materials used in that decision. Existing ordinary imprisonment alone is not the eligibility basis.

entries.custody_evidence: Multi-year continuation of segregation tied to political materials and organizing, supported by sworn testimony. Known released in May 2020 and deceased in 2022; no current custody inferred.

research_notes: Preserve every existing identity, field, biography and case. Only missing people are added. DOB for Jamaa is reconstructed from two contemporary family-interview reports, not estimated from an undated age. No prison release dates are inserted into these segregation cases, and no rounded year totals become exact counters. First-person allegations are attributed. The support links are actual personal sites. Coordinates are approximate Crescent City community markers, not a precise cell or institution location. Salinas Valley has no verified institution match in the database and is named in case prose; do not confuse Monterey County Jail with that prison. Paul Redd release-day sources differ (May 17, 21, 22); retain May 2020 in prose only. See audit for open leads and completed Beaver 55 roster check.
